children: Hindustan Copper rallied nearly 5% in Tuesday's trade after copper prices hit a fresh record high amid tight supplies and expectations of US tariffs on refined metal imports.
Hindustan Copper was trading 4.73% higher at Rs 533.20 as of 10:08 am on Tuesday.

Copper extended gains for a fourth straight session on the London Metal Exchange, touching a record $14,617 a tonne. Three-month copper futures were up 0.5% at $14,581 a tonne as of 11:08 am in Singapore. The metal has gained more than 17% this year.
Geojit retained a positive view on copper September futures, saying, "As long as prices stay above Rs 1300 positive bias are intact. Downside turnaround point is seen at Rs 1180."
Kotak Neo said LME base metals closed mixed, with copper setting a fresh record at $14,533 a tonne as supply constraints and tariff-driven inventory dislocations continued to tighten the market.

"Copper is up more than 17% this year, with structural support from ageing mine supply and rising demand from grids, data centres and electrification. However, the recent acceleration is increasingly a function of trade flows, expectations of US tariffs have drawn substantial metal into the US, reducing availability across the LME network and intensifying pressure on shorts," the brokerage said in its Tuesday commodity note.

Kotak Neo also flagged near-term supply risks after Chile's August copper exports fell to their lowest level in more than a year amid mine disruptions and severe weather. "With tariff policy still unresolved, copper should remain well supported, but stretched positioning and elevated prices leave the market increasingly vulnerable to demand weakness or a firmer dollar," it said.

Meanwhile, demand in China, the world's biggest copper consumer, is expected to pick up as the manufacturing sector enters its traditional peak season. Inventories in Shanghai Futures Exchange warehouses fell to their lowest level since 2024 last week.

"It should be easy for copper to reach $15,000," Jia Zheng, a trading manager at Suzhou Chuangyuan Harmony-Win Capital Management Co, told Bloomberg. Orders from State Grid Corp. of China are looking good, based on conversations with clients, she said.

Operational problems at major copper projects are also fuelling concerns over supply, with global mined production at risk of posting its first annual decline since 2017 unless output recovers in the second half.

title: Hindustan Copper rallies nearly 5% as copper breaches record high; Geojit sees further upside, here's what's driving the surge
